metadata.title: Unge, skole og demokrati: Hovedresultater af ICCS 2016

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICCS 2016 is an international large-scale survey administered to students in participating countries (8th grade/around age 14–15), with additional questionnaires for teachers and school leaders. The book reports international and national results using ICCS scaling procedures (Rasch-based scales) and compares country means and distributions; however, the provided text does not specify whether analysts applied student/sampling weights or replicate weights in the national reporting. Because ICCS is designed with complex sampling (students nested in schools and countries), appropriate weighting is typically required for population-representative estimates, but this manuscript excerpt does not document the exact weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate design method. Therefore, the weighting strategy cannot be verified from the excerpt, and any interpretation should treat the reported country comparisons as ICCS-standard estimates rather than explicitly weight-documented re-analyses.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report/book presents ICCS results using scaled scores and percentages derived from the ICCS assessment design, but the excerpt does not document a plausible-values (PV) workflow or any PV-based achievement modeling. The dependent outcomes are reported as Rasch-scaled scores and attitudinal/behavioral scales (e.g., political interest, trust, civic values) rather than explicitly as PV-based cognitive achievement estimates with a stated PV-combining procedure. Missing-data handling is therefore not transparently documented in the provided text, which is a reporting gap for methodological transparency.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The excerpt states that ICCS 2016 in Denmark is based on responses from approximately 6,500 students from more than 300 different 8th-grade classes across 185 schools. No further analytic inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., specific booklet/task completion filters, missing-data exclusions, or subsample restrictions) are described in the provided text; thus, the analytic sample is not further specified beyond the stated Denmark coverage.

data.outcome_summary: This Danish ICCS 2016 results volume summarizes international and Nordic patterns in civic and citizenship education among students in 8th grade (about age 14–15). The assessment includes a cognitive civic knowledge test (88 items across four content domains: social systems, democratic principles, political participation, and identity) administered via a booklet design where each student answers a subset of items; results are reported on an ICCS Rasch scale anchored to the ICCS 2009 metric (international mean 500, SD 100) and further described using performance levels (A–D plus below-D). Beyond test scores, the book reports attitudinal and behavioral scales (political interest, political self-efficacy, political conversations, media use, trust in institutions and people, global threat perceptions, and civic values/rights) and school-level participation indicators based on school leader and teacher surveys. The excerpt provides extensive descriptive comparisons (means, percentages, and changes from 2009 to 2016) but does not describe any predictive ML modeling, PV-combining procedure, or missing-data handling strategy.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The provided text is a national results/reporting book for ICCS 2016 rather than an empirical machine-learning study. It does not specify any ML algorithms, predictive targets, model evaluation metrics, or a data-analytic pipeline typical of ML papers. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty, while the outcome summary focuses on the assessment design and descriptive results reported in the text.
